title: Take it out of sight
header_line: Jose's analysis of a book we are still naming. Not a summary of the book. Not affiliated with or endorsed by the author or publisher.

lines.text: What is your relationship to the objects in your room?
A student said: being intentional about your environment was my resolution this year. It does not have to be big. In a single small room you can designate a chair.
A student said that chapter 7 is about elimination: removing a habit is easier if it is not in your direct line of sight.
Jose said: our behavior is not defined by the objects in the environment but by our relationship to them. So by taking the objects out of the environment, the relationship is gone.

He said this is very Jungian, and recalled a quote that until you make the unconscious conscious, you will not direct your life and you will call it fate. This is his recollection of the quote and needs a person to check it.
What is one object you could take out of sight this week?

exercise.title: Five minutes
steps: Write a habit you want to eliminate.
Write the object that triggers it.
Write where you could put it so you cannot see it.
Write what you will put in its place.
Write what you will notice after a week.

check.q: What did Jose say defines behavior?
What did a student say makes removing a habit easier?
choices: Not having it in your direct line of sight

check.q: What did a student say you can designate in a small room?

recap: Take the cue out of sight. Change your relationship to objects.
